title: Implement Dynamic Backend Routing based on Custom Request Headers
description: The Utility Nexus Gateway currently proxies all incoming API requests to a single, statically configured backend service defined in `app_config.ini`. To support A/B testing and canary deployments, a new feature is required to dynamically route requests to different backend services based on the value of a custom HTTP header. This task will require modifications across the configuration, core request handling logic, and API documentation over multiple development sessions.

project_spec.name: Utility Nexus Gateway
project_spec.description:
Utility Nexus Gateway is a medium-sized C-based REST + GraphQL service that centralises a collection of small but frequently needed utilities (hashing, data conversion, encryption helpers, date-time math, file metadata, etc.) behind a unified HTTP/GraphQL façade. Built on strict hexagonal architecture, the core utility algorithms live in an isolated domain layer, while protocols such as REST, GraphQL, and an API-Gateway façade are implemented as outer adapters. This separation lets teams reuse or replace the utility core in CLI tools, cron jobs, or even embedded environments without touching the perimeter. 

Externally, the service exposes classic REST endpoints for straightforward scripting and a single /graphql endpoint that provides flexible, typed queries and mutations generated from a GraphQL_Schema. Cross-cutting concerns—response_caching, rate_limiting, authentication, structured logging, monitoring metrics, and comprehensive error_handling—are all implemented as dedicated adapter plugs around the hexagon, keeping the domain layer free from infrastructural noise. The project includes auto-generated OpenAPI and GraphQL SDL documentation, making the service both self-describing and easy to integrate.
dependencies: libmicrohttpd (lightweight HTTP server for REST endpoints)
libgraphqlparser + cjsonschema (runtime GraphQL parsing and validation)
libev or libuv (event loop for non-blocking IO)
libcache (e.g., libmemcached or custom in-process LRU) for response_caching
libbloom or redis-bloom (rate_limiting token bucket adapter)
